summary.headline: Afcons posted its first-ever quarterly loss (Q4 net loss INR 89 crore) and FY26 PAT fell to INR 251 crore; no FY27 revenue or margin guidance given.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue fell 18% YoY to INR 2,777 crore and EBITDA dropped to INR 170 crore from INR 415 crore, with a net loss of INR 89 crore. Management blamed customer payment delays, overseas supply-chain disruption from the Middle East conflict, one-off provisions and marine cost overruns, and failure to cross margin-recognition thresholds on some projects. FY26 revenue was INR 12,322 crore (down 5.4%), EBITDA INR 1,439 crore (11.7% margin) and PAT INR 251 crore after a INR 76 crore Labour Code charge. Management guided FY26 order booking of INR 30,000 crore for FY27 but declined to give revenue or margin guidance until visibility improves.

segments.name: Overseas projects
segments.commentary: About 30% of FY26 turnover came from overseas, though overseas is only about 13% of the current order book; Q4 execution there was hit by fuel, gas and logistics disruption linked to the Middle East war, with materials routed via Dubai.

segments.name: Domestic projects
segments.commentary: Management estimated about 25% of domestic projects were affected in March; UP Jal Jeevan Mission payments are being withheld until 100% completion, against a contractual stage-wise payment basis.

segments.name: Other income
segments.commentary: FY26 other income of INR 374 crore is treated as operating income; of this, arbitration interest was INR 19 crore and other interest INR 61 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order booking guidance of INR 30,000 crore; about INR 15,000 crore is described as near-certain including L1 positions, with the balance to be won.
No revenue growth or EBITDA margin guidance for FY27 or Q1 FY27, citing geopolitical uncertainty, elongated award cycles and payment issues.
FY27 capex guided at about INR 725 crore; FY26 capex was INR 1,069 crore.
Management expects a sizable drop in debt in FY27, but warned that Q1 and Q2 debt typically rise.
Expects about INR 1,000 crore of stuck receivables to be liquidated by June 2026; working capital days (currently about 143) targeted at about 120 days, with no firm commitment beyond that.
Expects tunnelling to begin on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad HSR C2 package before the end of the next quarter, after the second TBM reached site.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR 1,069 crore, of which about INR 700 crore was in Q4; FY27 capex guided at about INR 725 crore.

FY26 depreciation included INR 454 crore accelerated depreciation on TBMs; normal depreciation about INR 289 crore; Q4 depreciation about INR 100 crore per quarter, expected to rise modestly in FY27 as TBM additions of about INR 1,000 crore hit gross block.
Mumbai-Ahmedabad HSR C2 tunnel boring machine second consignment received; tunnelling expected to start before end of next quarter, and the package may extend by 12-15 months.
HRRL crude oil terminal at Mundra commissioned in FY26; Bangalore double-decker metro and Delhi-Meerut RRTS sections operational.
demand_pricing: FY26 order inflow was INR 4,125 crore excluding about INR 3,800 crore of variation and change orders; intake was below plan due to deferred awards and slow L1 conversion.
Order book about INR 31,000-32,500 crore; about 80% government, split roughly 50% state and 50% central; states include Maharashtra, Uttarakhand, MP, Rajasthan, UP and Bihar.

Since 31 March: about INR 8,000 crore of orders secured, including Croatia railway (about INR 7,544 crore) and DMRC underground metro (INR 373 crore); L1 positions of about INR 7,000 crore including Vadhavan (about INR 5,300 crore).

Two Croatia road tenders where Afcons was L1 were cancelled by the client on budget grounds; Pune Ring Road and Nagpur-Gondiya L1 positions were removed after rebid instructions, with Pune Ring Road possibly re-tendered around June.
Bid pipeline about INR 4 lakh crore over two years (70% domestic, 30% overseas); FY27 INR 30,000 crore mix stated as about 60% domestic and 40% international.

Domestic contracts carry escalation formulas (steel, cement, labour, fuel); overseas contracts mostly fixed-price with internal contingency. Croatia contract absorbs up to 10% cost increase, with pass-through above that.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 so far below the mid-quarter confidence expressed on the Q3 call, and what drove the miss?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q4 customer payments did not come as in the past 15-20 years; Afcons chose liquidity over growth, funding projects only up to limits, and overseas supply disruption in March (fuel, gas, logistics) hit execution.

qa_highlights.question: What are the one-off items in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Total one-offs of about INR 260-265 crore: about INR 160 crore of Q4 provisions (including an ECL matrix shift), a significant arbitration-related provision, and extra cost on a marine project. Management said no further provisions were made in Q1 FY27 to date.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of finance cost and the rise in interest?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40% of customer advances in FY26 were interest-bearing versus a partial-year effect in FY25; average borrowing rose and rate cuts did not fully offset the increase.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the order book and receivables are affected by payment delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Payment delays are widespread; apart from UP Jal Jeevan Mission and a Gabon project, no specific names were disclosed. Projects below 10% completion carry about two months of receivables.

qa_highlights.question: Why no guidance when order book is about INR 60,000 crore after inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited long gestation projects (four dams of about five years; HSR package extended 12-15 months), elongated award cycles, and fuel and geopolitical uncertainty, saying revenue visibility is not yet adequate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Gabon bank guarantee impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Gabon bank guarantee invoked and paid; the contract was already loss-provided with no margin recognised, and about 92% complete.

risks_watch: Receivable collections: about INR 1,000 crore unlock expected by June; working capital days at about 143 versus 120-day target.
Interest-bearing customer advances (about 40% of advances) keep finance cost elevated while margins are not yet recognised on several projects.
Overseas execution (about 30% of turnover) exposed to fuel, gas and logistics disruption; fixed-price contracts with limited pass-through.
Order conversion: about INR 7,000 crore of L1 positions still to convert; Pune Ring Road and Nagpur-Gondiya rebidding; further Croatia-type cancellations possible.
Govt. payment delays (UP Jal Jeevan Mission, state treasury) and labour availability/cost under the new Labour Code.
Debt trajectory: management expects a sizable FY27 debt reduction, but Q1-Q2 debt typically rises.
summary.management_tone: Defensive and apologetic at the outset, with the MD saying he is personally upset; the CFO's answers were detailed on one-offs but evasive on forward payments and margins, repeatedly declining guidance pending visibility.
key_quotes: I apologize to all the investors that we have made a loss in the quarter for the first time since we started publishing quarterly numbers from 2010.

Having a certainty of about INR 15,000 crores order including L1 in the current financial year, we expect to book another INR 15,000 crores of more orders, making a total order booking guidance of INR 30,000 crores for the current financial year.

At this stage, considering the continued uncertainty in the geopolitical environment, elongated award cycles and ongoing project-related developments, we believe it would be prudent to wait for greater visibility before providing specific revenue growth or EBITDA margin guidance for FY27.
